choices.text: Alkalemia and sodium/volume loading
choices.explanation: These follow from excess buffer and sodium administration.

choices.text: Acidemia and loss of administered sodium
choices.explanation: This reverses the principal direction of effect.

choices.text: Vitamin-K depletion and platelet blockade
choices.explanation: These are antithrombotic mechanisms, not bicarbonate effects.

choices.text: Bronchodilation and suppression of airway inflammation
choices.explanation: These are respiratory drug effects.

questions.point: Excess bicarbonate can cause alkalemia and sodium/volume load.

questions.stem: Before sodium bicarbonate administration, which pair must be reconciled against the actual product and order?

choices.text: Tablet coating and dietary fiber grams
choices.explanation: These do not determine an IV bicarbonate dose.

choices.text: Concentration and ordered mEq
choices.explanation: Percentage, mL, and mEq cannot be treated as interchangeable labels.

choices.text: Inhaler actuation count and inspiratory flow
choices.explanation: These refer to an inhaled device.

choices.text: Sublingual dissolution time and tablet score
choices.explanation: These do not establish the IV buffer preparation.

questions.point: Read concentration and ordered units from the actual emergency product.

questions.stem: During arrest, no specific metabolic or toxicologic indication for bicarbonate has been identified. Why is a routine dose not assumed?

choices.text: Bicarbonate is the treatment that electrically converts asystole
choices.explanation: Asystole is not electrically converted this way.

choices.text: Bicarbonate is the first-line antiarrhythmic for every shockable rhythm
choices.explanation: This is not its routine algorithm role.

choices.text: Added sodium and alkali may not treat the arrest’s cause
choices.explanation: Its role is selected and does not replace core arrest care.

choices.text: Bicarbonate directly improves oxygen delivery regardless of ventilation
choices.explanation: It does not replace ventilation or cause-directed care.

questions.point: Bicarbonate is not routine treatment for undifferentiated cardiac arrest.

questions.stem: Two IV medicines are due through one line, but compatibility of the actual preparations is unknown. What information resolves the mixing question?

choices.text: The fact that both medicines are used in emergencies
choices.explanation: Clinical use does not determine physical or chemical compatibility.

choices.text: The fact that both medicines are prescribed intravenously
choices.explanation: A shared route does not establish chemical compatibility.

choices.text: The fact that both medicines are clear solutions
choices.explanation: Visual clarity before mixing does not establish compatibility.

choices.text: Verified compatibility for those products and concentrations
choices.explanation: Compatibility depends on the actual preparation and administration conditions.

questions.point: IV compatibility must be verified for the exact medicines and preparation.
